title: Manhattan plot

blocks.what_we_do: Plot association evidence along the autosomal genome.
blocks.why: A Manhattan plot places chromosome and position on the horizontal axis and -log10(p) vertically. Nearby high points can be correlated through LD and may represent one region. Position identifies where evidence is observed, not which gene causes an effect. The axis uses GRCh38 throughout. Alternating colours separate chromosomes; chromosome labels and position order also carry that information.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-3}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
plot_data <- results
plot_data$CHROM <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(plot_data$CHROM))
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.3", "manhattan.png"), function() plot_manhattan(plot_data, "Simulated GWAS: age, sex and ten PCs"))
stopifnot(sum(results$P[valid_p(results$P)] < 5e-8) == 8L)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
Three strong regions on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12, comprising eight variants below 5e-8. The moderate planted region does not reach that conventional threshold. Non-autosomal tests remain in the result table but are not placed on this autosomal figure.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Do four nearby significant variants necessarily imply four independent causal effects?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. LD can make several tested variants tag the same underlying signal.

</details>

figures.gemini_prompt: Draw a schematic Manhattan plot with clearly labelled chromosomes and the conventional 5e-8 line. Mark a group of correlated points as one region, and state that a peak does not identify a causal gene. Do not invent gene annotations.
figures.alt_text: Autosomal association peaks exceed the conventional threshold on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12.
